objects.description: Opaque handle to a libmagic context used to load magic databases and query file, descriptor, or buffer types. It is a typedef to a pointer to an incomplete struct magic_set, keeping the implementation hidden.

Incomplete (opaque) struct representing the internal state and configuration for libmagic operations. Only a forward declaration is present in this header; the structure layout is private to the implementation.

functions.name: magic_open
functions.description: Create and initialize a libmagic handle for subsequent file/buffer type detection. The flags argument enables behavior bits (MAGIC_*). Typical usage: call magic_open, then magic_load/compile to load a magic database, then magic_file/magic_buffer to query, and finally magic_close.
requirements: flags must be 0 or a bitwise OR of supported MAGIC_* constants defined in this header.
The returned magic_t must be checked for NULL to detect allocation/initialization failure.
The returned handle must be closed with magic_close when no longer needed before being discarded.
The handle is required for all other magic_* functions that take a magic_t.

functions.name: magic_close
functions.description: Release and invalidate a libmagic handle previously obtained by magic_open, freeing associated resources.
requirements: ms must be a valid magic_t previously returned by magic_open.
After this call, ms must not be used in any subsequent magic_* calls.

functions.name: magic_getpath
functions.description: Return a filesystem path string to a magic database. If a specific magicfile path is provided, it may be returned or used to resolve a path; otherwise a default path may be chosen. Exact behavior of flags is unspecified in this header; consult implementation. Returns a const, NUL-terminated string or NULL on error.
requirements: If magicfile is non-NULL, it must point to a valid, NUL-terminated string path.
flags is an integer; acceptable values are unspecified here (likely 0 or MAGIC_* bits).
Caller must treat the returned pointer as read-only and must not free it.
Caller must check for NULL to detect failure.

functions.name: magic_file
functions.description: Analyze the named file and return a textual description (or MIME/other selected info based on flags in the handle). Returns a const string on success or NULL on error.
requirements: ms must be a valid handle created by magic_open and not yet closed.
A magic database should be loaded into ms via magic_load or magic_compile before calling, otherwise detection may fail.
filename must point to a valid, NUL-terminated path string to a file accessible to the process.
Caller must check for NULL return and may call magic_error/ms + magic_errno for details.
The returned string must be treated as read-only and not freed by the caller.

functions.name: magic_descriptor
functions.description: Analyze the content available via an open file descriptor and return a textual description (or MIME/other info depending on flags). Returns a const string on success or NULL on error.
requirements: ms must be a valid handle created by magic_open and not yet closed.
A magic database should be loaded into ms via magic_load or magic_compile before calling, otherwise detection may fail.
fd must be a valid open file descriptor that the process can read from.
Caller must check for NULL return and may use magic_error/magic_errno for diagnostics.
The returned string must be treated as read-only and not freed by the caller.

functions.name: magic_buffer
functions.signature: const char *magic_buffer(magic_t ms, const void *buffer, size_t length);
functions.description: Analyze an in-memory buffer of length bytes and return a textual description (or MIME/other info based on flags). Returns a const string on success or NULL on error.
requirements: ms must be a valid handle created by magic_open and not yet closed.
A magic database should be loaded into ms via magic_load or magic_compile before calling, otherwise detection may fail.
buffer must point to at least length bytes of readable memory; if length is 0, behavior is implementation-defined.
Caller must check for NULL return and may use magic_error/magic_errno for diagnostics.
The returned string must be treated as read-only and not freed by the caller.

functions.name: magic_error
functions.description: Return a human-readable error message string associated with the most recent failure on the given handle, or NULL if no error message is available.
requirements: ms must be a valid handle created by magic_open and not yet closed.
The returned string must be treated as read-only and not freed by the caller.

functions.name: magic_getflags
functions.description: Get the current option flags associated with the handle (bitwise OR of MAGIC_* constants).
requirements: ms must be a valid handle created by magic_open and not yet closed.

functions.name: magic_setflags
functions.description: Set option flags on the handle (bitwise OR of MAGIC_* constants) to control output and behavior (e.g., MIME, follow symlinks). Returns an int status; exact success/failure convention is not specified in this header.
requirements: ms must be a valid handle created by magic_open and not yet closed.
flags must be 0 or a bitwise OR of the supported MAGIC_* constants defined in this header.
Caller must check the return value for failure; exact semantics (e.g., 0 or -1 for error) are unspecified here.

functions.name: magic_version
functions.description: Return the library version number as an integer (compare with MAGIC_VERSION).

functions.name: magic_load
functions.description: Load a magic database into the handle from the specified path, making the handle ready to classify data. Returns an int status; exact success/failure convention is not specified in this header.
requirements: ms must be a valid handle created by magic_open and not yet closed.
magicfile must be a valid, NUL-terminated path to a magic database file; exact handling of NULL is unspecified here.
This function should be called (or magic_compile) before magic_file/magic_descriptor/magic_buffer for meaningful results.
Caller must check the return value for failure; use magic_error/magic_errno for details.

functions.name: magic_load_buffers
functions.signature: int magic_load_buffers(magic_t ms, void **bufs, size_t *sizes, size_t nbufs);
functions.description: Load one or more magic databases from memory buffers into the handle. The buffers represent compiled or source magic data (exact format unspecified here). Returns an int status; exact success/failure convention is not specified in this header.
requirements: ms must be a valid handle created by magic_open and not yet closed.
bufs must point to an array of nbufs buffer pointers; each bufs[i] must point to readable memory holding a magic database blob.
sizes must point to an array of nbufs sizes; sizes[i] must be the byte length of bufs[i].
nbufs specifies the number of entries in bufs and sizes; they must be consistent.
Caller must check the return value for failure; use magic_error/magic_errno for details.

functions.name: magic_compile
functions.description: Compile the specified magic file into a binary database (or prepare it for use) associated with the handle. Returns an int status; exact success/failure convention is not specified in this header.
requirements: ms must be a valid handle created by magic_open and not yet closed.
magicfile must be a valid, NUL-terminated path to a magic source file; exact handling of NULL is unspecified here.
Caller must check the return value for failure; use magic_error/magic_errno for details.

functions.name: magic_check
functions.description: Check the specified magic file for correctness/consistency. Returns an int status; exact success/failure convention is not specified in this header.
requirements: ms must be a valid handle created by magic_open and not yet closed.
magicfile must be a valid, NUL-terminated path to a magic file; exact handling of NULL is unspecified here.
Caller must check the return value for failure; use magic_error/magic_errno for details.

functions.name: magic_list
functions.description: List the entries in the specified magic file. Output destination and exact format are unspecified in this header. Returns an int status; exact success/failure convention is not specified here.
requirements: ms must be a valid handle created by magic_open and not yet closed.
magicfile must be a valid, NUL-terminated path to a magic file; exact handling of NULL is unspecified here.
Caller must check the return value for failure.

functions.name: magic_errno
functions.description: Return an error code (errno-style) associated with the most recent failure on the given handle.
requirements: ms must be a valid handle created by magic_open and not yet closed.

functions.name: magic_setparam
functions.signature: int magic_setparam(magic_t ms, int param, const void *val);
functions.description: Set a tunable parameter on the handle. The param selects which parameter to set (see MAGIC_PARAM_* constants). The val points to the value to set; the expected pointed-to type/size depends on param and is not specified in this header. Returns an int status; exact success/failure convention is not specified here.
requirements: ms must be a valid handle created by magic_open and not yet closed.
param must be one of the MAGIC_PARAM_* constants defined in this header.
val must point to a value of the correct type and size for the chosen param; the required type/size are unspecified here and must match implementation expectations.
Caller must check the return value for failure; use magic_error/magic_errno for details.

functions.name: magic_getparam
functions.signature: int magic_getparam(magic_t ms, int param, void *val);
functions.description: Retrieve a tunable parameter from the handle. The param selects which parameter to query (see MAGIC_PARAM_* constants). The val points to storage for the result; the expected pointed-to type/size depends on param and is not specified in this header. Returns an int status; exact success/failure convention is not specified here.
requirements: ms must be a valid handle created by magic_open and not yet closed.
param must be one of the MAGIC_PARAM_* constants defined in this header.
val must point to writable storage of the correct type and sufficient size for the chosen param; the required type/size are unspecified here and must match implementation expectations.
Caller must check the return value for failure; use magic_error/magic_errno for details.

data_types.description: A NUL-terminated string representing a filesystem path to a file. It may be absolute or relative and can include any bytes valid for paths on the target OS, excluding embedded NUL.
The contents of a file at the provided path, treated as uninterpreted bytes. No specific format is required; any binary or text content is valid.
A memory buffer of arbitrary bytes of a specified length. No encoding or structure is assumed; may include any byte values.
On-disk libmagic database file (compiled magic). Typically produced by magic_compile or provided by the system. Binary format understood by libmagic; used by magic_load.

In-memory representation of one or more libmagic databases provided as raw byte buffers alongside their sizes, suitable for consumption by magic_load_buffers. Equivalent to the bytes of compiled magic files.
Textual libmagic rules source (uncompiled). Contains pattern rules as understood by file(1)/libmagic. Used by magic_compile, magic_check, and magic_list.

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces a bytes object that represents a single NUL-terminated
# filesystem path string. The fuzzing harness uses FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() and
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR() to obtain file path strings; we therefore generate a wide
# variety of valid, interesting path patterns that are still valid on common
# POSIX-like systems and many Windows path parsers used in cross-platform code.
#
# Notes:
# - We avoid embedding NUL except for the required terminator.
# - Paths are ≤ 4096 bytes.
# - We include absolute/relative, dot segments, symlink-like components, spaces,
#   unicode, long components, and typical file extensions that libmagic can
#   recognize to encourage the fuzzer to open realistic files.
# - Although the harness may map the filename to random file content, the path
#   itself should be syntactically valid and diverse.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

POSIX_SEP = "/"
WIN_SEP = "\\\\"

# Some interesting directory names/components
DOT_COMPONENTS = [".", "..", ".", ".."]
COMMON_DIRS = [
    "tmp", "var", "usr", "home", "etc", "opt", "lib", "bin", "dev", "mnt",
    "proc", "sys", "run", "srv", "local", "share", "cache", "config",
]
SPECIAL_NAMES = [
    "con", "nul", "prn", "aux", "com1", "lpt1",  # Windows reserved names
    "中文", "データ", "данные", "données", "datos", "data", "Δεδομένα",
    "sp ace", "tab\tsep", "newline\nsep", "semi;colon", "col:on",
]

# Common file basenames and extensions that libmagic recognizes
BASENAMES = [
    "README", "LICENSE", "Makefile", "configure", "a.out", "core",
    "image", "video", "audio", "document", "archive", "index",
]
EXTS = [
    # archives
    "tar", "gz", "bz2", "xz", "zip", "7z", "rar", "zst",
    # executables & libs
    "so", "dll", "dylib", "exe", "elf", "o", "a",
    # images
    "png", "jpg", "jpeg", "gif", "bmp", "tiff", "ico", "webp",
    # audio/video
    "mp3", "flac", "wav", "ogg", "mp4", "mkv", "avi", "mov",
    # docs
    "pdf", "ps", "rtf", "doc", "docx", "xls", "xlsx", "ppt", "pptx",
    # text/code
    "txt", "md", "json", "xml", "yaml", "yml", "ini", "csv", "html", "htm",
    "c", "h", "cc", "cpp", "hpp", "py", "sh", "lua", "rb", "go", "rs",
    # db
    "sqlite", "db", "db3",
]

# Filenames that look like magic database sources/compiled
MAGIC_NAMES = [
    "magic", "magic.mgc", "magic.mime", "mime.mgc", "usr/share/misc/magic.mgc",
]

UNICODE_CHARS = [
    "ä", "ß", "ñ", "ø", "å", "é", "í", "ó", "ú", "ç", "ő", "ű",
    "漢", "字", "한", "글", "🙂", "Ω", "π", "µ",
]

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_"


def _rand(r: random.Random, seq: List[str]):
    return seq[r.randrange(len(seq))]


def _random_component(r: random.Random) -> str:
    kind = r.randrange(6)
    if kind == 0:
        # simple safe token
        length = r.randint(1, 20)
        return ''.join(r.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(length))
    if kind == 1:
        # include unicode
        base = ''.join(r.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(r.randint(1, 8)))
        uni = ''.join(r.choice(UNICODE_CHARS) for _ in range(r.randint(1, 3)))
        return base + uni
    if kind == 2:
        return _rand(r, COMMON_DIRS)
    if kind == 3:
        return _rand(r, SPECIAL_NAMES)
    if kind == 4:
        # long component to test limits
        length = r.randint(50, 150)
        return ''.join(r.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(length))
    # dot components
    return _rand(r, DOT_COMPONENTS)


def _random_filename(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Sometimes choose explicit magic paths
    if r.random() < 0.15:
        name = _rand(r, MAGIC_NAMES)
    else:
        base = _rand(r, BASENAMES) if r.random() < 0.5 else _random_component(r)
        # Optional second dot segment
        if r.random() < 0.2:
            base += "." + _rand(r, EXTTS := EXTS)  # keep chance for double extension
        ext = _rand(r, EXTS)
        name = f"{base}.{ext}"
    return name


def _build_posix_path(r: random.Random) -> str:
    parts: List[str] = []
    # absolute or relative
    absolute = r.random() < 0.5
    n = r.randint(1, 8)
    for i in range(n - 1):
        parts.append(_random_component(r))
    parts.append(_random_filename(r))
    # Optionally inject repeated slashes
    sep = POSIX_SEP if r.random() < 0.8 else POSIX_SEP * r.randint(2, 4)
    path = sep.join(parts)
    if absolute:
        path = POSIX_SEP + path
    # Optionally trailing slash (rare for files but valid path string)
    if r.random() < 0.1:
        path += POSIX_SEP
    return path


def _build_windows_path(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Drive letter or UNC
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        # UNC path
        server = _random_component(r)
        share = _random_component(r)
        prefix = f"{WIN_SEP}{WIN_SEP}{server}{WIN_SEP}{share}"
    else:
        drive = r.choice(string.ascii_letters)
        prefix = f"{drive}:" + WIN_SEP
    parts: List[str] = []
    n = r.randint(1, 6)
    for i in range(n - 1):
        parts.append(_random_component(r))
    parts.append(_random_filename(r))
    sep = WIN_SEP
    path = prefix + sep.join(parts)
    return path


def _maybe_env_prefix(r: random.Random, path: str) -> str:
    # Occasionally prefix with environment variable or tilde expansion
    choice = r.random()
    if choice < 0.15:
        var = _rand(r, ["HOME", "USER", "TMP", "TEMP", "APPDATA", "LOCALAPPDATA"]) \
              if r.random() < 0.6 else _random_component(r).upper()
        return f"${{{var}}}/" + path
    if choice < 0.30:
        # Tilde variants
        user = "" if r.random() < 0.7 else _random_component(r)
        return f"~{user}/" + path
    return path


def _ensure_limit(path: str) -> str:
    # Truncate to stay within MAX_TOTAL-1 for NUL terminator
    max_len = MAX_TOTAL - 1
    if len(path.encode('utf-8', 'surrogatepass')) <= max_len:
        return path
    # Trim safely at character boundary by reducing characters
    trimmed = path
    while len(trimmed.encode('utf-8', 'surrogatepass')) > max_len and trimmed:
        trimmed = trimmed[:-1]
    return trimmed if trimmed else "a"


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose platform style
    style = r.randrange(3)
    if style == 0:
        path = _build_posix_path(r)
        path = _maybe_env_prefix(r, path)
    elif style == 1:
        path = _build_windows_path(r)
    else:
        # Mixed separators to exercise normalization logic in callers
        p = _build_posix_path(r)
        # Randomly replace some slashes with backslashes
        path_chars = []
        for ch in p:
            if ch == '/' and r.random() < 0.3:
                path_chars.append('\\\\')
            else:
                path_chars.append(ch)
        path = ''.join(path_chars)
    path = _ensure_limit(path)
    # Encode as UTF-8 and append NUL terminator as required by C APIs
    b = path.encode('utf-8', 'surrogatepass') + b"\x00"
    # Final guard
    if len(b) > MAX_TOTAL:
        b = b[:MAX_TOTAL-1] + b"\x00"
    return b

import random
import struct
import zlib

# This generator produces valid, interesting file contents for libmagic's magic_file.
# It targets a wide variety of recognizable formats and edge cases, while ensuring
# each output is a coherent, valid file blob (not mutated corruption).

MAX_SIZE = 4096

_rng = None

def _seed_rng(seed: int):
    global _rng
    _rng = random.Random(seed)

def _rand_bytes(n: int) -> bytes:
    return _rng.randbytes(n) if hasattr(_rng, 'randbytes') else bytes(_rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

def _pick(seq):
    return seq[_rng.randrange(len(seq))]

# Generators for various recognizable file formats

def gen_elf() -> bytes:
    # Minimal 64-bit or 32-bit ELF header with no sections (still recognizable)
    is64 = _rng.choice([True, False])
    endian = _rng.choice([1, 2])  # 1=little, 2=big
    ei_class = 2 if is64 else 1
    e_ident = b"\x7fELF" + bytes([ei_class, endian, 1, 0]) + bytes(12)  # EI_VERSION=1
    def pack(fmt_le, fmt_be, *vals):
        fmt = fmt_le if endian == 1 else fmt_be
        return struct.pack(fmt, *vals)
    if is64:
        e_type = _pick([2, 3, 1])  # EXEC, DYN, REL
        e_machine = _pick([62, 3, 40, 183])  # x86_64, x86, ARM, AArch64
        header = pack('<HHI', '>HHI', e_type, e_machine, 1)
        e_entry = 0
        e_phoff = 64
        e_shoff = 0
        e_flags = 0
        e_ehsize = 64
        e_phentsize = 56
        e_phnum = 1
        e_shentsize = 64
        e_shnum = 0
        e_shstrndx = 0
        rest = pack('<QQQIHHHHHH', '>QQQIHHHHHH', e_entry, e_phoff, e_shoff, e_flags,
                    e_ehsize, e_phentsize, e_phnum, e_shentsize, e_shnum, e_shstrndx)
        # Minimal PT_LOAD program header
        p_type = 1  # PT_LOAD
        p_flags = 5  # R+X
        p_offset = 0
        p_vaddr = 0x400000
        p_paddr = 0
        p_filesz = 64
        p_memsz = 64
        p_align = 0x200000
        phdr = pack('<IIQQQQQQ', '>IIQQQQQQ', p_type, p_flags, p_offset, p_vaddr, p_paddr, p_filesz, p_memsz, p_align)
        blob = e_ident + header + rest + phdr
        return blob
    else:
        e_type = _pick([2, 3, 1])
        e_machine = _pick([3, 40])
        header = pack('<HHI', '>HHI', e_type, e_machine, 1)
        e_entry = 0
        e_phoff = 52
        e_shoff = 0
        e_flags = 0
        e_ehsize = 52
        e_phentsize = 32
        e_phnum = 1
        e_shentsize = 40
        e_shnum = 0
        e_shstrndx = 0
        rest = pack('<IIIIHHHHHH', '>IIIIHHHHHH', e_entry, e_phoff, e_shoff, e_flags,
                    e_ehsize, e_phentsize, e_phnum, e_shentsize, e_shnum, e_shstrndx)
        # Program header 32-bit
        p_type = 1
        p_offset = 0
        p_vaddr = 0x8048000
        p_paddr = 0
        p_filesz = 52
        p_memsz = 52
        p_flags = 5
        p_align = 0x1000
        phdr = pack('<IIIIIIII', '>IIIIIIII', p_type, p_offset, p_vaddr, p_paddr, p_filesz, p_memsz, p_flags, p_align)
        return e_ident + header + rest + phdr

def gen_png() -> bytes:
    # Minimal PNG with IHDR, IDAT (compressed empty), IEND
    sig = b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n"
    def chunk(typ: bytes, data: bytes) -> bytes:
        return struct.pack('>I', len(data)) + typ + data + struct.pack('>I', zlib.crc32(typ + data) & 0xffffffff)
    width = _rng.choice([1, 2, 16, 256])
    height = _rng.choice([1, 2, 16, 256])
    bit_depth = _rng.choice([8])
    color_type = _rng.choice([2, 6, 0, 3])
    ihdr = struct.pack('>IIBBBBB', width, height, bit_depth, color_type, 0, 0, 0)
    bpp = {0:1,2:3,3:1,4:2,6:4}[color_type] * bit_depth // 8
    row = b"\x00" + (b"\x00" * (width * bpp))
    raw = row * height
    comp = zlib.compress(raw)
    data = sig + chunk(b'IHDR', ihdr) + chunk(b'IDAT', comp) + chunk(b'IEND', b'')
    return data

def gen_gzip() -> bytes:
    payload_len = min(_rng.randint(0, 512), MAX_SIZE)
    payload = _rand_bytes(payload_len)
    # GZIP header: ID1 ID2 CM FLG MTIME XFL OS
    hdr = b"\x1f\x8b\x08\x00" + b"\x00\x00\x00\x00" + b"\x02\xff"
    compobj = zlib.compressobj(level=6, wbits=-15)
    deflated = compobj.compress(payload) + compobj.flush()
    crc = zlib.crc32(payload) & 0xffffffff
    isize = len(payload) & 0xffffffff
    return hdr + deflated + struct.pack('<II', crc, isize)

def gen_zip() -> bytes:
    # Minimal ZIP with one uncompressed file
    name = _pick([b"a.txt", b"bin", b"folder/file.dat"])
    data = _rand_bytes(_rng.randint(0, 128))
    dos_time = 0x0000
    dos_date = 0x0000
    crc = zlib.crc32(data) & 0xffffffff
    comp_size = len(data)
    uncomp_size = len(data)
    version_needed = 20
    general_flag = 0
    method = 0  # store
    file_comment = b""
    local_header_offset = 0

    # Local file header
    lf_hdr = (
        b"PK\x03\x04" +
        struct.pack('<HHHHHIIIHH', version_needed, general_flag, method, dos_time, dos_date,
                    crc, comp_size, uncomp_size, len(name), len(file_comment)) +
        name + file_comment + data
    )

    # Central directory header (fixed fields layout)
    version_made_by = 20
    internal_attr = 0
    external_attr = 0
    cd_hdr = (
        b"PK\x01\x02" +
        struct.pack(
            '<HHHHHHIIIHHHHHII',
            version_made_by,      # version made by
            version_needed,       # version needed
            general_flag,         # general purpose bit flag
            method,               # compression method
            dos_time,             # last mod file time
            dos_date,             # last mod file date
            crc,                  # crc-32
            comp_size,            # compressed size
            uncomp_size,          # uncompressed size
            len(name),            # file name length
            0,                    # extra field length
            0,                    # file comment length
            0,                    # disk number start
            internal_attr,        # internal file attributes
            external_attr,        # external file attributes
            local_header_offset   # relative offset of local header
        ) +
        name
    )

    # End of central directory
    cd_offset = len(lf_hdr)
    cd_size = len(cd_hdr)
    eocd = b"PK\x05\x06" + struct.pack('<HHHHIIH', 0, 0, 1, 1, cd_size, cd_offset, 0)
    return lf_hdr + cd_hdr + eocd

def gen_pdf() -> bytes:
    ver = _pick([b"1.3", b"1.4", b"1.7"])
    xref = b"xref\n0 1\n0000000000 65535 f \n"
    trailer = b"trailer\n<< /Size 1 /Root 1 0 R >>\nstartxref\n0\n%%EOF\n"
    obj = b"1 0 obj\n<< /Type /Catalog >>\nendobj\n"
    return b"%PDF-" + ver + b"\n" + obj + xref + trailer

def gen_tar() -> bytes:
    # USTAR header for one empty file
    name = _pick([b"file", b"test.txt", b"dir/file.bin"])[:100]
    def chksum(hdr):
        s = sum(hdr[:148]) + sum(b"        ") + sum(hdr[156:])
        return s
    hdr = bytearray(512)
    hdr[0:len(name)] = name
    hdr[100:108] = b"0000644"  # mode
    hdr[108:116] = b"0000000"  # uid
    hdr[116:124] = b"0000000"  # gid
    hdr[124:136] = b"00000000000"  # size octal (0)
    hdr[136:148] = b"00000000000"  # mtime
    hdr[156:157] = b"0"  # typeflag file
    hdr[257:263] = b"ustar\x00"
    hdr[263:265] = b"00"
    csum = chksum(hdr)
    hdr[148:156] = (oct(csum)[2:]).encode().rjust(6, b"0")[:6]
    hdr[154:156] = b"\x00 "
    return bytes(hdr) + b"\x00" * 1024  # EOF blocks

def gen_ar() -> bytes:
    # Unix archive (ar) with one member
    sig = b"!<arch>\n"
    name = b"file.o/".ljust(16)
    mtime = b"0".rjust(12)
    uid = b"0".rjust(6)
    gid = b"0".rjust(6)
    mode = b"100644".rjust(8)
    data = b"OBJ"
    size = str(len(data)).encode().rjust(10)
    hdr = name + mtime + uid + gid + mode + size + b"`\n"
    return sig + hdr + data + (b"\n" if len(data) % 2 else b"")

def gen_pe() -> bytes:
    # Minimal PE/COFF header recognizable
    mz = b"MZ" + b"\x90\x00\x03\x00\x00\x00\x04\x00" + b"\x00" * 18 + struct.pack('<I', 0x80)
    pe = b"PE\x00\x00"
    machine = _pick([0x14c, 0x8664])
    number_sections = 0
    time = 0
    symptr = 0
    numsym = 0
    opt_size = 0xE0 if machine == 0x14c else 0xF0
    characteristics = 0x0002
    coff = struct.pack('<HHIIIHH', machine, number_sections, time, symptr, numsym, opt_size, characteristics)
    opt_magic = 0x10b if machine == 0x14c else 0x20b
    opt = struct.pack('<H', opt_magic) + b"\x00" * (opt_size - 2)
    return mz + b"\x00" * (0x80 - len(mz)) + pe + coff + opt

def gen_text() -> bytes:
    choices = [
        b"#!/bin/sh\necho hello\n",
        b"#!/usr/bin/env python3\nprint('hi')\n",
        b"int main(){return 0;}\n",
        b"<html><head><title>T</title></head><body>Hi</body></html>\n",
        b"; SQL\nSELECT 1;\n",
    ]
    s = _pick(choices)
    if _rng.random() < 0.3:
        s = b"\xef\xbb\xbf" + s
    return s

def gen_json() -> bytes:
    objs = [
        b'{"key": "value"}',
        b'[1, 2, 3]',
        b'{"nested": {"a": 1}, "arr": [true, false, null]}'
    ]
    return _pick(objs)

def gen_xml() -> bytes:
    return b"<?xml version=\"1.0\"?><root attr=\"v\"><child/></root>\n"

def gen_jpeg() -> bytes:
    soi = b"\xff\xd8"
    app0 = b"\xff\xe0" + struct.pack('>H', 16) + b"JFIF\x00\x01\x02\x00\x00\x01\x00\x01\x00\x00"
    dqt = b"\xff\xdb" + struct.pack('>H', 67) + b"\x00" + bytes(range(1, 65))
    sof0 = b"\xff\xc0" + struct.pack('>H', 17) + b"\x08\x00\x10\x00\x10\x01\x01\x11\x00"
    dht = b"\xff\xc4" + struct.pack('>H', 0x1f) + b"\x00" + b"\x00" * (0x1f - 2)
    sos = b"\xff\xda" + struct.pack('>H', 12) + b"\x01\x01\x00\x00\x3f\x00"
    eoi = b"\xff\xd9"
    entropy = b"\x00\x3f\x00\x00\x00"
    return soi + app0 + dqt + sof0 + dht + sos + entropy + eoi

def gen_bmp() -> bytes:
    width = _rng.choice([1, 2, 16])
    height = _rng.choice([1, 2, 16])
    bpp = 24
    row = ((width * 3 + 3) // 4) * 4
    pix = row * height
    bfType = b"BM"
    bfOffBits = 54
    bfSize = bfOffBits + pix
    filehdr = bfType + struct.pack('<IHHI', bfSize, 0, 0, bfOffBits)
    infohdr = struct.pack('<IIIHHIIIIII', 40, width, height, 1, bpp, 0, pix, 2835, 2835, 0, 0)
    data = b"\x00" * pix
    return filehdr + infohdr + data

def gen_gif() -> bytes:
    header = _pick([b"GIF87a", b"GIF89a"])
    w = _rng.choice([1, 2, 16])
    h = _rng.choice([1, 2, 16])
    lsd = struct.pack('<HHB', w, h, 0x80) + b"\x00\x00"
    gct = b"\x00\x00\x00" * 2
    img_desc = b"\x2C" + struct.pack('<HHHHB', 0, 0, w, h, 0x00)
    img_data = b"\x02\x02\x4C\x01\x00"
    trailer = b"\x3B"
    return header + lsd + gct + img_desc + img_data + trailer

def gen_lua() -> bytes:
    sig = b"\x1bLua"
    ver = _pick([0x51, 0x52, 0x53, 0x54])
    header = bytes([ver, 0x00, 0x01, 0x04, 0x04, 0x04, 0x08, 0x00])
    return sig + header + b"\x00" * 16

def gen_wasm() -> bytes:
    magic = b"\x00asm"
    version = struct.pack('<I', 1)
    return magic + version

def gen_ascii_prop() -> bytes:
    lines = [
        b"# comment\n",
        b"key=value\n",
        b"path=/usr/bin\n",
        b"enabled=true\n",
    ]
    return b"".join(lines)

FORMATS = [
    gen_elf, gen_png, gen_gzip, gen_zip, gen_pdf, gen_tar, gen_ar, gen_pe,
    gen_text, gen_json, gen_xml, gen_jpeg, gen_bmp, gen_gif, gen_lua, gen_wasm, gen_ascii_prop
]

def _maybe_truncate(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    if len(data) <= MAX_SIZE:
        return data
    return data[:MAX_SIZE]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    """
    Generate a valid, interesting file content buffer suitable for magic_file input.
    The content type is chosen pseudo-randomly based on seed, and each format
    generator strives to produce syntactically valid, recognizable data.
    """
    _seed_rng(seed)
    gen = _pick(FORMATS)
    data = gen()
    if _rng.random() < 0.2 and len(data) < MAX_SIZE:
        pad_len = _rng.randint(0, min(64, MAX_SIZE - len(data)))
        data += _rand_bytes(pad_len)
    return _maybe_truncate(data)

import random
from typing import List

"""
This generator produces a valid libmagic source magic file (text format),
which magic_load() can parse. We build a compact set of rules covering various
features, with randomized but valid content. The output is under 4 KiB.
"""

_SIMPLE_MIME_TYPES = [
    ("application/octet-stream", "bin"),
    ("text/plain", "txt"),
    ("image/png", "png"),
    ("image/jpeg", "jpg"),
    ("application/zip", "zip"),
    ("application/pdf", "pdf"),
]

_TEXT_SAMPLES = [
    "Alpha", "Beta", "Gamma", "Delta", "Epsilon",
    "hello", "world", "magic", "libmagic", "fuzz",
]

_DEF_WORDS = ["the", "hello", "TODO", "NOTE", "function"]

def _rand_bytes(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(r.randrange(0, 256) for _ in range(n))

def _escape_magic_string_literal(b: bytes) -> str:
    # Magic source uses tab-separated fields; escape tabs and backslashes.
    s = b.decode('latin1', errors='ignore')
    s = s.replace('\\', r'\\').replace('\t', r'\t')
    return s

def _rand_text(r: random.Random) -> str:
    k = r.randint(1, min(3, len(_TEXT_SAMPLES)))
    parts = r.sample(_TEXT_SAMPLES, k=k)
    s = " ".join(parts)
    s = s.replace('\\', r'\\').replace('\t', r'\t')
    return s

def _gen_magic_source(r: random.Random) -> str:
    lines: List[str] = []

    # Header comment
    lines.append("# Generated magic source for fuzz seeding")

    # Rule 1: Identify a custom signature at offset 0 and use a subroutine
    sig = _rand_bytes(r, 4)
    desc = _rand_text(r)
    mime, ext = r.choice(_SIMPLE_MIME_TYPES)
    sig_lit = _escape_magic_string_literal(sig)
    lines.append("0\tstring\t" + sig_lit + "\tCustomSig: " + desc)
    lines.append(">&0\tuse\tcustom-sub")

    # Subroutine 'custom-sub'
    rnd_short = r.randrange(0, 0xFFFF)
    rnd_long = r.randrange(0, 0xFFFFFFFF)
    lines.append("!:name\tcustom-sub")
    lines.append(">4\tbelong\t0x%08x\tlevel2" % rnd_long)
    lines.append(">>2\tbeshort\t0x%04x\tlevel3" % rnd_short)

    # Rule 2: ELF header
    lines.append("0\tstring\t\x7fELF\tELF executable")
    lines.append(">16\tbyte\t>=\t1\tELF class 32/64")

    # Rule 3: ZIP header
    lines.append("0\tstring\tPK\x03\x04\tZIP archive data")
    lines.append(">30\tubyte\t=\t0\tstored or deflated")

    # Rule 4: PNG signature
    lines.append("0\tstring\t\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n\tPNG image data")

    # Rule 5: Text regex
    word = r.choice(_DEF_WORDS)
    lines.append("0\tregex\t" + word + "\tText containing '" + word + "'")

    # Rule 6: Indirect offset example
    lines.append("0\tbeshort\t>0\tHas offset indirection")
    lines.append(">&0\tstring\tID\tFound ID tag at computed offset")

    # Global MIME and ext hints
    lines.append("!:mime\t" + mime)
    lines.append("!:ext\t" + ext)

    # Rule 7: PDF header (avoid %-formatting by building string pieces)
    pdf_ver_major = r.randint(1, 2)
    pdf_ver_minor = r.randint(0, 7)
    lines.append("0\tstring\t" + "%PDF-" + str(pdf_ver_major) + "." + str(pdf_ver_minor) + "\tPDF document")

    # Rule 8: JPEG SOI
    lines.append("0\tbeshort\t0xffd8\tJPEG image data")

    # Rule 9: ASCII/UTF-8 printable regex
    lines.append("0\tregex\t^[\x09\x0a\x0d\x20-\x7e]+$\tASCII/UTF-8 text")

    # Rule 10: PE/DOS header then PE header presence
    lines.append("0\tstring\tMZ\tDOS/PE executable")
    lines.append(">0x3c\tlelong\t>0\tPE header present")

    src = "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
    if len(src) > 4000:
        src = src[:4000] + "\n"
    return src

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    src = _gen_magic_source(r)
    return src.encode('utf-8', errors='surrogatepass')

# Generator for libmagic compiled database blobs (approximate but valid-enough)
# Strategy:
# - Produce one or more buffers that resemble compiled magic databases.
# - Real compiled databases are binary, little-endian, and contain multiple
#   entries. We approximate with a recognizable header, followed by a sequence
#   of records containing offsets, types, and test strings or numeric tests.
# - While we cannot reproduce the exact private on-disk format, many libmagic
#   builds also accept textual magic source through magic_load_buffers when the
#   implementation supports parsing. To maximize validity, we generate textual
#   magic source lines terminated by newlines, grouped into plausible sections.
# - The fuzzer stub passes our bytes directly; providing UTF-8 text with
#   correctly formatted magic rules increases the chance of successful loads.
#
# We will therefore emit textual magic(5) source content, which commonly looks like:
#   0   string      %PDF-      PDF document
#   >4  string      %EOF       trailer
#   0   beshort     0x4D5A     MS-DOS executable
# including continuations using '>' and MIME types via !:mime and strength tweaks.
#
# We randomize across multiple small databases to exercise multi-buffer loading.

TEXT_RULE_SNIPPETS = [
    # Simple string signatures at offset 0
    "0	string	%PDF-\tPDF document\n!:mime	application/pdf\n",
    "0	string	PK\x03\x04\tZip archive data\n!:mime	application/zip\n",
    "0	string	\x7fELF\tELF executable\n!:mime	application/x-elf\n",
    "0	string	%PNG\r\n\x1a\n\tPNG image data\n!:mime	image/png\n",
    "0	string	GIF89a\tGIF image data\n!:mime	image/gif\n",
    # PE/COFF via MZ then PE at offset from header

    "0	string	\xff\xd8\xff\tJPEG image data\n!:mime	image/jpeg\n",
    # Tar

    "!:apple \"ttxt\"\n",
]

def _rand_magic_source(rng: random.Random, max_lines: int) -> str:
    lines: List[str] = []
    # Pick 1-3 primary rules
    primaries = rng.sample(TEXT_RULE_SNIPPETS, k=rng.randint(1, min(3, len(TEXT_RULE_SNIPPETS))))
    lines.extend(primaries)
    # Maybe add some numeric rules
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        lines.append(rng.choice(NUMERIC_RULE_SNIPPETS))
    # Add some continuations under some primaries
    for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 3)):
        lines.append(rng.choice(CONTINUATIONS))
    # Occasionally add generic MIME hints or strength tweaks
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        lines.append(rng.choice(MIME_HINTS))
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        lines.append(rng.choice(ENCODING_LINES))
    # Limit total lines roughly
    text = ''.join(lines)
    # Ensure newline termination
    if not text.endswith('\n'):
        text += '\n'
    # Cap size
    return text[:2048]

def _make_database_blob(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Prefer textual magic source for higher likelihood of acceptance.
    text = _rand_magic_source(rng, max_lines=32)
    return text.encode('utf-8')

def _maybe_concat_blobs(rng: random.Random, blobs: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    # Sometimes concatenate multiple magic sources separated by newlines to simulate a bigger db
    if len(blobs) == 1:
        return blobs[0]
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        sep = b"\n\n"
        out = sep.join(blobs)
        return out[:4096]
    return blobs[0]

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Generate between 1 and 3 buffers worth of textual magic content.
    n = rng.randint(1, 3)
    blobs = [_make_database_blob(rng) for _ in range(n)]
    # Sometimes combine them to produce a single larger blob; otherwise return first.
    result = _maybe_concat_blobs(rng, blobs)
    # Ensure non-empty and within size limit
    if not result:
        result = b"0\tstring\tDATA\tdata\n"
    return result[:4096]

import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# This generator produces a textual libmagic source file (uncompiled) suitable
# for use with magic_compile, magic_check, and magic_list. It aims to cover a
# variety of rule features while staying valid and parseable by libmagic.

MAGIC_HEADER = "# Magic file auto-generated for fuzz seeding\n# Encoding: utf-8\n\n"

# Representative MIME types, charsets, and strengths
MIME_TYPES = [
    "application/octet-stream",
    "text/plain",
    "image/png",
    "image/jpeg",
    "application/zip",
    "application/pdf",
    "application/x-executable",
]
CHARSETS = ["binary", "us-ascii", "utf-8", "iso-8859-1"]

# Some common file signatures to build valid and diverse tests
SIGS = [
    (0, "string", "%PDF-", "PDF document"),
    (0, "string", "\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n", "PNG image"),
    (0, "string", "PK\x03\x04", "ZIP archive"),
    (0, "string", "\xff\xd8\xff", "JPEG image"),
    (0, "string", "ELF", "ELF binary"),
    (257, "string", "ustar", "POSIX tar archive"),
]

# Some indirect/cstring/regex features to exercise parser
REGEXES = [
    (0, "regex", br"^#!.*\b(sh|bash|python|perl)\b", "script text"),
    (0, "regex", br"^\%\!PS-Adobe-\d+\.\d+", "PostScript"),
]

# Helper to escape bytes for magic string type (C-style escapes acceptable)
def escape_bytes_for_magic(data: bytes) -> str:
    out = []
    for b in data:
        if 32 <= b <= 126 and b not in (0x5c, 0x22):  # printable except \ and "
            out.append(chr(b))
        elif b == 0x5c:
            out.append("\\\\")
        elif b == 0x22:
            out.append('\\"')
        elif b == 0x0a:
            out.append("\\n")
        elif b == 0x0d:
            out.append("\\r")
        elif b == 0x09:
            out.append("\\t")
        else:
            out.append(f"\\x{b:02x}")
    return ''.join(out)

# Build a single magic rule line
# Format: offset  type  test  message  (with optional > continuations)

def rule_line(offset: int, mtype: str, test: str, message: str, mime: str | None = None,
              strength: int | None = None, charset: str | None = None) -> List[str]:
    lines = []
    base = f"{offset}\t{mtype}\t{test}\t{message}"
    lines.append(base)
    if mime:
        lines.append(f">\tmime\t{mime}")
    if charset:
        lines.append(f">\tchar\tcharset={charset}")
    if strength is not None:
        lines.append(f">\tname\tstrength={strength}")
    return lines

# Create diverse numeric/integer tests with masks and endianness
INT_TYPES = [
    ("byte", 1),
    ("short", 2),
    ("beshort", 2),
    ("leshort", 2),
    ("long", 4),
    ("belong", 4),
    ("lelong", 4),
    ("quad", 8),
    ("bequad", 8),
    ("lequad", 8),
]

COMPARATORS = ["=", "<", ">", "&"]

DESCRIPTORS = [
    "binary data",
    "little-endian value",
    "big-endian value",
    "masked match",
]

# Some text encodings and use of search/cstring to exercise features
TEXT_SAMPLES = [
    (0, "search/256", "TODO:", "contains TODO"),
    (0, "search/4096", "function ", "contains keyword"),
    (0, "string", "#!/", "shebang-like"),
    (0, "cstring", "main", "C symbol"),
]

# Create a small magic section with name for grouping
SECTION_NAMES = ["generic", "archives", "images", "documents", "executables", "text"]


def build_magic(seed: int) -> str:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    lines: List[str] = [MAGIC_HEADER.rstrip()]  # will add blank lines explicitly

    # Global default and name sections to exercise headers
    lines.append(f"# Random seed {seed}")
    lines.append("!:strength +5")
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        lines.append("!:mime")
    lines.append("")

    # Named sections
    for sec in rnd.sample(SECTION_NAMES, k=rnd.randint(3, min(5, len(SECTION_NAMES)))):
        lines.append(f"# {sec} section")
        lines.append(f"0\tname\t{sec}")
        lines.append("")

    # Signature-based rules
    for off, mtype, sig, msg in rnd.sample(SIGS, k=rnd.randint(3, len(SIGS))):
        esc = escape_bytes_for_magic(sig.encode('latin1') if isinstance(sig, str) else sig)
        mime = rnd.choice(MIME_TYPES) if rnd.random() < 0.8 else None
        charset = rnd.choice(CHARSETS) if rnd.random() < 0.3 else None
        strength = rnd.randint(10, 80) if rnd.random() < 0.5 else None
        lines.extend(rule_line(off, "string", esc, msg, mime=mime, strength=strength, charset=charset))
        lines.append("")

    # Regex-based rules
    for off, mtype, pattern, msg in REGEXES:
        # regex pattern is in bytes; escape appropriately as C-string in magic
        esc = escape_bytes_for_magic(pattern)
        mime = rnd.choice(MIME_TYPES) if rnd.random() < 0.5 else None
        lines.extend(rule_line(off, "regex", esc, msg, mime=mime))
        lines.append("")

    # Integer and masked tests with continuations
    for _ in range(rnd.randint(4, 8)):
        typ, size = rnd.choice(INT_TYPES)
        off = rnd.choice([0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32])
        comp = rnd.choice(COMPARATORS)
        if comp == "&":
            mask = 1 << rnd.randint(0, size * 8 - 1)
            test = f"&0x{mask:x}"
            msg = rnd.choice(DESCRIPTORS)
        else:
            val = rnd.getrandbits(size * 8)
            test = f"{comp}{val}"
            msg = rnd.choice(DESCRIPTORS)
        base = f"{off}\t{typ}\t{test}\t{msg}"
        lines.append(base)
        # Add one or two continuations
        if rnd.random() < 0.7:
            lines.append(">\tstring\tASCII\tpossible text")
        if rnd.random() < 0.4:
            lines.append(">>\tbyte\t=0\tterminator")
        if rnd.random() < 0.4:
            lines.append(">\tmime\tapplication/octet-stream")
        lines.append("")

    # Text/substring rules
    for off, t, s, msg in TEXT_SAMPLES:
        esc = escape_bytes_for_magic(s.encode('utf-8'))
        lines.extend(rule_line(off, t, esc, msg, mime="text/plain"))
        lines.append("")

    # Indirect offset demonstration: use indirect to look up length-prefixed data
    # Format: at offset 0, a 2-byte length (le), then check string at computed offset
    lines.append("0\tleshort\t>0\tlen prefix")
    lines.append(">\tindirect\t0.l\tindirect-start")
    lines.append(">>\tstring\tDATA\tlen-prefixed DATA")
    lines.append("")

    # Use use/name to define and reference a subtest
    lines.append("0\tname\tblock-A")
    lines.append(">0\tstring\tHEAD\tblk header")
    lines.append("0\tuse\tblock-A")
    lines.append("")

    # Default catch-alls with priority tweak
    lines.append("0\tstring\t\x00\x00\x00\x00\tNULs")
    lines.append(">\tmime\tapplication/octet-stream")
    lines.append("!:strength -5")

    # Ensure newline termination
    text = "\n".join(lines)
    if not text.endswith("\n"):
        text += "\n"
    # Limit to 4096 bytes
    return text[:4096]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    text = build_magic(seed)
    return text.encode("utf-8")
